learned.claim: v0.6.2 closes audit gap #1: advisory session lease (append-only guard), CHAIN FORKED detection with loud full stop, and a history-preserving leaf merge whose salvage is scanned at merge time.
An advisory lock must fail OPEN on corruption (warn and proceed) while integrity chains fail CLOSED - opposite polarities in one subsystem, each correct for its job.
The lease guards chain APPEND only: prune funnels through the next guarded checkpoint and merge operates where the lease already failed - guarding them is ceremony without protection.

verify cannot distinguish a forged-but-well-formed head from an honest one; merge authority is the operator's choice plus git provenance - an honestly documented limit, with mandatory post-merge verify as the backstop.
First test failures were the lease correctly refusing the test's own second session - a guard that fires before its tests exist is a good sign the design is load-bearing.
